_why: Mutant ids declared BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING for sigma, each with the measurement behind it. `vit_mutate.py --equivalences` reads the KEYS of this object, so the claim and its reason live in one file, and a declared mutant LEAVES THE DENOMINATOR -- every entry is a claim somebody has to be able to answer. THREE are declared, and all three are the `CHARACTER(:), ALLOCATABLE` staging-buffer idiom this campaign has now reached in FIVE units (ReadAvrSWAP, ExtController, UpdateZeroMQ, interp1d, sigma). NOT ONE of them is in the arithmetic: the whole cubic, both clamps, all four coefficients and every literal in them were killed by the corpus, 42 of 45 behavioural mutants, including the two `negate_cond` mutants on the clamps that the KERNEL cannot see at all (see evidence/sigma/README.md). The undeclared run is committed beside this file at 0.933 (mutation/sigma.undeclared.json), so what survived is on the record before it was excused. AND THE THREE ARE NOT ONE CLAIM: 532e4d37 is EQUIVALENT and proved exhaustively over the whole type; the other two are UNREACHABLE OVER THIS CORPUS, which is a blind spot and says so.
532e4d37: compare_op '>' -> '>=' at `n > 0 ? static_cast<size_t>(n) : 0` in `errmsg_trim`. EQUIVALENT, and proved EXHAUSTIVE OVER THE WHOLE TYPE rather than over the corpus: the two spellings can differ only where the predicate does, at `n == 0`, and there the tight form yields the literal `0` and the loose form `static_cast<size_t>(0)` -- the same view length. evidence/sigma/equivalence_probe.{cpp,txt} sweeps all 4,294,967,296 values a 32-bit `int` admits through both spellings and reports 0 at which the resulting length differs, with INT32_MIN, -1, 0, 1 and INT32_MAX printed as witnesses. This is the strongest of the three: it holds on every input the C type has, not merely on the ones this campaign generates. SAME SITE, SAME PROOF as interp1d's b61327db -- re-run here rather than cited, because a measurement taken on another unit's source is a measurement of that unit.
2524b715: const_tweak '0' -> '1' at the SAME line -- `n > 0 ? static_cast<size_t>(n) : 0` becomes `... : 1`, so an ErrMsg field arriving with a non-positive length would be read as one byte instead of none. UNREACHABLE HERE, and measured rather than reasoned: evidence/sigma/errmsg_extremes_probe.{cpp,txt} is the shipped translation with counters and nothing else changed, run over all 1,069 harness cases -- `ErrVar->n_ErrMsg on entry, min .. max  1 .. 8`, `calls with n_ErrMsg <= 0: 0` in 1,069 calls. THIS IS A BLIND SPOT AND NOT AN EQUIVALENCE, and the difference is stated rather than blurred: the `0` branch is the view's own NOT-ALLOCATED convention (`VIT_CHAR_UNALLOCATED` is -1 in vit_types.h) and the generator has no rung that puts a CHARACTER extent at its unallocated sentinel or at zero. Not taken inside this unit, for the reason interp1d recorded and this unit inherits unchanged: the character-length ladder is an EXISTING block in harness/generate.py, and a rung added there shifts the random draws of every unit already scored (X3). DECISIONS.md, still a candidate.
7ad82e7d: compare_op '>' -> '>=' at `if (static_cast<int>(s.size()) > ErrVar->n_ErrMsg_cap)` in `assign_errmsg`. The two forms differ on exactly one input, `s.size() == n_ErrMsg_cap`, where the loose form refuses an assignment that exactly fits. MEASURED over the corpus by the same probe: `ErrVar->n_ErrMsg_cap, min .. max  4097 .. 4104`, `largest message offered to assign_errmsg  14`, `calls with s.size() == cap: 0` in 1,022 assignments. UNREACHABLE, not equivalent. The capacity is `LEN(ErrMsg) + 4096` in the differential harness (harness/emit.py ALLOC_HEADROOM) and the same 4096 in the integrated build (vit_errorvariables_view.f90); this unit's ONLY message is `'sigma:' // TRIM(ErrMsg)`, so its length is the incoming length plus six and the guard is true in every configuration this campaign can build. What is DIFFERENT here from the four earlier units carrying this site: their messages are literals of fixed length, so the guard was unreachable by construction; this one's message GROWS with its input, so the guard is unreachable only because the corpus does not supply an ErrMsg within six characters of the buffer -- a weaker claim, and it is stated as the weaker one. SAME SITE, SAME DECLARATION as ReadAvrSWAP's e82a5f90, ExtController's 11d2c9cc, UpdateZeroMQ's ac7a5b72 and interp1d's e34d5cc4. NOT REMOVED: the guard is what makes an over-long assignment a REFUSAL rather than a truncation, and a truncated error message is the one wrong answer a bit comparison cannot catch.
